hints.S42_A1: The sentence turns on BUT: the skill SEEMED IMPOSSIBLE, and yet he kept WATCHING TUTORIALS AND PRACTISING DAILY. Ask: which verb means to keep trying despite difficulty? 'Gave up' is its exact opposite.
hints.S42_A2: The student held the VIOLIN BOW CORRECTLY FOR THE FIRST TIME - that is good news. Ask: which verb means to tell someone they have done well? 'Scolded' tells them off, and 'ignored' says nothing at all.
hints.S42_A3: AFTER MONTHS OF PRACTICE she can now PERFORM IN FRONT OF A SMALL AUDIENCE. Ask: did her skills climb or fall? 'Faded', 'collapsed' and 'disappeared' all point downwards.
hints.S42_A4: The instructor DEMONSTRATED the technique first, and the students must follow it STEP BY STEP. Ask: which verb means to copy exactly what you were shown? 'Invent' would create something new instead.
hints.S42_A5: Great learners LEARN FROM FAILURE and keep going. Ask: what feeling must they avoid? Choose the one word that would stop a person trying again - 'motivated', 'inspired' and 'rewarded' all push you forward.
hints.S42_B1: HAS is waiting for a partner, and FOR THREE YEARS runs right up to today. Ask: after 'has', which form builds a present perfect - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle?
hints.S42_B2: The POWER CUT SUDDENLY KNOCKED OUT the computers - one sharp event landing in the middle of something longer. Ask: which choice shows work already going on at that past moment?
hints.S42_B3: FAR needs a comparative to lean on, and THAN compares coding with how it LOOKS. Ask: is 'easy' a short adjective that takes -er, or a long one needing a comparing word? 'Easily' is an adverb and cannot follow 'far'.
hints.S42_B4: PATIENCE cannot be counted - there is no plural - and THAN sets one amount against another. Ask: which quantity word compares two amounts of an uncountable thing? 'Many', 'a few' and 'several' need countable nouns.
hints.S42_B5: The statement is already NEGATIVE, and it is built in the present perfect (YET is the clue). Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag flip to positive or stay negative? The tag must reuse the same helping verb, so 'did' is out.
hints.S42_B6: Read both halves: learning it online and learning it in a CLASSROOM were equal in DIFFICULT work - neither harder nor easier. Ask: which pair of words builds an EQUAL comparison? 'More ... than' says one side wins.
hints.S42_B7: The POTTERY PIECES did not walk to the EXHIBITION - somebody put them there, and the subject is plural. Ask: which choice is passive, with the subject receiving the action, and set in the past?
hints.S42_B8: The instructor is FORBIDDING one reaction and offering another instead - TRY AGAIN. Ask: after 'told + person', does the verb stay plain, take -ing, or follow the little word before an infinitive? And where does the negative word sit?
hints.S42_C1: The mistake may or may not happen, and the advice - DO NOT GIVE UP - follows only when it does. Ask: which joining word introduces a plain, open condition? A precaution word would mean you act beforehand.
hints.S42_C2: Read the first half: YOU CANNOT IMPROVE - it is already negative. Ask: which joining word carries a hidden negative inside itself, meaning 'except when'? Adding a plain condition word would reverse the sense.
hints.S42_C3: The two halves clash: learning something new can be FRUSTRATING, and yet the FEELING OF SUCCESS makes it worthwhile. Ask: does the joining word show a reason, or a contrast between two facts that pull opposite ways?
hints.S42_C4: Nothing clashes here: wanting a place in the SCHOOL ORCHESTRA is exactly WHY Rina kept practising. Ask: does the second half fight the first, or explain it? A contrast word would spoil the sense.
hints.S42_C5: The word TWICE measures how much time Ben spent, set beside Rina. Ask: which box phrase compares the DURATION of two people's practice? Nothing here is called better or worse - only longer or shorter.
hints.S42_C6: The teacher slows down deliberately, aiming at one result: NOBODY IS LEFT BEHIND. Ask: does the second half give a reason, or a PURPOSE - what he wants to achieve? Pick the phrase which introduces purpose.
hints.S42_C7: You cannot fetch a NOTEBOOK once the demonstration has begun - you carry it beforehand, just as a precaution. Ask: which phrase means 'as a precaution, because it might happen'? A plain condition would mean you act only when it does.
hints.S42_C8: The pattern is 'NOT ___ ... BUT ...' - two possibilities set side by side, and the second one wins. Ask: which joining word introduces a choice between two possibilities and can be followed by 'or not'?
hints.S42_D1: The clue is THE MOST BASIC STEPS CAN SEEM CONFUSING, and the blank follows 'a complete'. Ask: which box word names a person right at the start of learning? 'Discipline' and 'mastery' are things, not people.
hints.S42_D2: The dash defines it: THE ABILITY TO SHOW UP AND PRACTISE EVEN WHEN YOU DO NOT FEEL LIKE IT. Ask: which box word names that inner strength? 'Technique' is about how you do a thing, not whether you turn up.
hints.S42_D3: The examples follow the colon: HOW TO HOLD A PAINTBRUSH, HOW TO POSITION THE HANDS on a piano. Ask: which box word names the correct method for a task? After 'the correct' it must be a noun.
hints.S42_D4: The clue is UNTIL THEY BEGIN TO FEEL AUTOMATIC - the methods sink in and become part of you. Ask: which box word is a verb here, after 'the more naturally you'? A noun cannot fill this blank.
hints.S42_D5: TRUE ___ TAKES YEARS, and it stands above every small improvement. Ask: which box word names the highest level of skill? 'Beginner' names the lowest, and 'discipline' is only the habit that gets you there.
hints.S42_E1: The underlined word is short for 'they are', but the SKILLS belong to the students. Ask: can you replace it with 'they are' and still make sense? If not, drop the apostrophe and use the possessive spelling.
hints.S42_E2: The subject is THE STUDENTS - many of them, not one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past verb or the plural one? Match the verb to the subject, never to the nearest noun.
hints.S42_E3: IMPROVED is an action verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW the handwriting improved. Ask: does an action take an adjective, or an adverb ending in -ly? 'Noticeably' beside it is your model.
hints.S42_E4: The BEST PIECES belong to the pupils - more than one owner. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only number? For plural owners, where does the apostrophe sit: before the -s, or after it?
hints.S42_E5: 'Good' refuses the -er ending, exactly as 'bad' does. Ask: what is the comparative of 'good'? It is an irregular word that changes shape completely, and GOODER is never English.
hints.S42_F1: Sentence A is the condition: you START WITH THE SIMPLEST TECHNIQUES. Ask: after a condition phrase, does the verb take 'will', or stay in the simple present? Only the second half - the promise - looks to the future.
hints.S42_F2: The two facts pull against each other: cooking SEEMED IMPOSSIBLE AT FIRST, yet Mia now cooks for the whole family. Ask: which fact follows the contrast word, and where does the comma fall? The impressive result stays in the main clause.
